articles.headline: Why Packers can't protect Jordan Love or rush successfully
articles.description: The two-year demise of the Packers' offensive line began on March 10, 2025 and has no end in sight.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The beginning of the downfall of the Green Bay Packers' offensive line can be traced to a specific day: March 10, 2025.

That was when general manager Brian Gutekunst signed then-San Francisco 49ers guard Aaron Banks to a four-year, $77 million free agent deal. Not only have the Packers not gotten their money's worth out of Banks due to injuries and poor performance, but his signing set in a motion a game of musical chairs at just about every position on the line.

The end result was what the Packers put on display in their most recent showing, the obliteration of their pass protection by the Minnesota Vikings in Sunday's 30-10 loss at Lambeau Field. In between that March 2025 day and Sunday has been 20 months of trying to get the offensive line settled.

Combine that with a position coach, Luke Butkus, and an offensive coordinator, Adam Stenavich, who have come under fire, and there's plenty of blame to go around for nearly two seasons' worth of offensive line issues.

"I think it's easy to pinpoint and point the finger and everybody wants to pinpoint blame, but the blame can go to everybody," coach Matt LaFleur said this week. "It's all of us in this together. Certainly it starts with myself and then it goes to everybody else. It's coaches and players collectively."

Don't forget about Gutekunst.

He started all this by signing Banks, who had played all but six of his 2,464 snaps for the 49ers at left guard. The problem was the Packers already had a left guard. A two-time Pro Bowl left guard in Elgton Jenkins. To accommodate Banks, the Packers moved Jenkins to center for the 2025 season. From a business perspective, Jenkins wasn't thrilled with it and sat out part of the offseason program in the hope that the team would adjust his contract. Jenkins eventually returned without a new deal, fractured his lower leg halfway through last season and was released in March.

In theory, Jenkins could have still been the Packers' left guard for this season had they never signed Banks because Jenkins had one year left on his contract when he was cut.

This season, the Packers have started four different left guards -- Banks, Donovan Jennings, Jager Burton and Laken Tomlinson. In all, they've started seven different guards, counting the three at right guard (Jacob Monk, Travis Glover and Tomlinson). It would have been eight had Kevin Zeitler not sustained a triceps injury in practice late last week. The in-season addition was set to start at right guard with Tomlinson back at left guard. Instead, the Packers went back to Glover at right guard.

That means Banks, who took home $29 million last season and will make $18 million this season, not only wasn't viewed as the best option at his natural left guard spot but couldn't beat out Glover, a 2024 sixth-round pick who missed all of last season because of a shoulder injury.

articles.headline: A Rams bye means time for rest and ramping up
articles.description: The bye "represents an opportunity to get recharged," but it also allows the team to improve.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- As Matthew Stafford relaxes and recovers during his bye week, the Los Angeles Rams quarterback has learned to expect a few texts from his head coach.

Stafford and Sean McVay are headed into their sixth bye week together, and the quarterback knows how his head coach likes to use the time.

"We'll definitely be texting with each other [and] talking to each other about how we move forward and how we try to help this team become the best version of itself," Stafford said.

While the bye "represents an opportunity to get recharged [and] refreshed," McVay said Sunday after the Rams' victory over the Arizona Cardinals that it also allows him to think about how he can continue to tweak and improve his offense.

"What are the new iterations that you want to try to be able to build on or creatively come up with new ideas based on who's available and who's not," McVay said. "And so I know that'll be helpful for me for sure. It's an accelerated bye, but I am excited about what this group has done."

McVay showed what might have been only a glimpse of that creativity in Week 10, when he had to game plan without wide receiver Puka Nacua (knee/toe). The Rams were also without veteran receiver Davante Adams (hamstring) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (hamstring/ankle).

Without their top two receivers, the Rams ran only three plays out of 11 personnel (three receivers on the field). Entering the game, they had run 53% of their plays this season out of that offensive grouping.

While the Rams still leaned in to 13 personnel (three tight ends on the field) against the Cardinals, they also ran plays out of two personnel groupings they had not all season. The Rams ran 17 plays out of 20 personnel (two running backs). According to NFL Next Gen Stats, the Rams totaled 197 yards and a touchdown on those plays. They also ran a play out of 21 personnel (two running backs, one tight end).

Since Adams injured a hamstring in Week 6, the Rams have leaned on their running game, led by the tandem of Blake Corum and Kyren Williams. During the four games without Adams, the Rams have outrushed their opponents 653-175 (478). According to ESPN Research, that is the team's largest rushing yards differential over a four-game span since 1984, the season Eric Dickerson ran for 2,105 yards.

Without Adams and Nacua on Sunday, the Rams rushed for 202 yards, including 100 rushing yards and a touchdown for Corum. It was Corum's sixth straight game with a touchdown, and it came on a day the running back had a career-high 20 touches. For much of the season, Corum and Williams have split carries and both had success.

After the game, Corum said he thought being in the backfield at the same time as Williams "was amazing."

"It felt great," Corum said. "I was super excited. We share a backfield, but actually to be on the field together, I wish I was in the Cardinals' minds to see what they thought."

articles.headline: Three-win Saints, Kellen Moore face defining stretch of games
articles.description: Starting with the Bears on Sunday, the head coach's tenure and the team's season sits at a crucial crossroads.
articles.body:
NEW ORLEANS -- The Saints (3-6) have a hill to climb if they want to get back to the top of the NFC South. At this point in the season, it almost feels insurmountable.

The Saints had an opportunity to secure first place in a shaky division last Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, however, they repeated many of their old mistakes, losing 20-17 after allowing two late scores.

"Obviously we had plenty of opportunities in this game. We didn't get it done," a terse Saints coach Kellen Moore said postgame, mentioning the need to "get better," four times.

But despite Moore repeating that phrase not just on Sunday but many times over the course of this rocky season, the Saints have failed to get better in key areas. Against the Panthers, New Orleans fell short in those areas again.

They didn't score points in the first quarter for the seventh time this season, an issue Saints rookie Jordyn Tyson noted Moore has "harped on," without results. They had less than 100 net rushing yards for the sixth time and had at least two turnovers for the fifth time this season.

The Saints now have an 0-2 record in the division and the feeling that they beat themselves yet again. Tight end Juwan Johnson said the Saints still believe things can be turned around, especially in a division in which no team has a winning record.

"What we could all do is to learn from it, watch the film, move forward," Johnson said of Sunday's loss. "I know it sounds like a PR answer, but that's literally what we have to do in order to move forward because we say it every year, we're only a game back."

While the Saints are only a few games out of contention now, that could easily slip away in the next few weeks. Not only do they have to account for those repeated mistakes that lost them games, but they have to fix them against some of the toughest opponents left on the schedule.

"We definitely knew [what] was at stake," Saints running back Travis Etienne Jr said. "So it wasn't like we was unaware and it definitely hurt that we didn't capitalize on that moment. Win that game, we would've had control of our own destiny. So I feel like now we're putting our faith in someone else's hands."

The next three games will be the most challenging stretch they've seen so far. The Saints will play at Chicago on Sunday (1 p.m. ET, Fox) against Dennis Allen's seventh-ranked Bears defense and at Cincinnati against the Bengals' top-ranked passing offense and top-scoring offense. Then, in Week 13, the Saints will host the Green Bay Packers, who have the second-ranked passing offense and a fourth-ranked scoring offense.

If the Saints lose all three of those games, they'll have a 3-9 record and a losing season for the second straight year under Moore. It would drop the head coach's overall record to 9-20 and a win percentage of 31%, way behind former Saints coach Mike Ditka (1997-99), who was fired after a 3-13 season in 1999 and a 15-33 coaching record in New Orleans.

articles.headline: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's top moments at Arrowhead Stadium
articles.description: Kelce's greatest Arrowhead moments include his first catch, lots of playoff magic, and meeting the love of his life, Taylor Swift.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Travis Kelce gets goosebumps every time, even though the drive from his home to his place of employment, at this point in his 14-year career, is routine.

On game days, his car enters Gate 5, the road that leads to the entrance of the Kansas City Chiefs' training facility. The destination of his journey always makes Kelce smile.

"You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere," Kelce said recently. "That's the best feeling for me."

Few players in the Chiefs' 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team's red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history -- joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt -- to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public.

Whenever Kelce's illustrious career ends -- which could happen after this season -- he will be remembered for being one of the franchise's greatest players and at minimum a three-time Super Bowl champion. He is also proud that his play, and most of his memorable highlights, will be synonymous with the history of Arrowhead, which is expected to have its final season in 2030.

"The fans love to fill that stadium and create those memories and get away from the realities of what the world is," Kelce said. "I just love the fact that they pour so much into it. It just makes you want to play that much harder for them. That definitely makes Arrowhead special."

Chiefs founder Lamar Hunt always said Arrowhead was his favorite place on earth. Kelce, 37, understands why Hunt, who died in 2006, had such a fond sentiment. Hours before kickoff, the expansive parking lots that surround the stadium host thousands of tailgating fans, many of them cooking the city's favorite cuisine: barbecue.

When driving into the stadium, Kelce often rolls down his windows to enjoy the tantalizing smell of the many cookouts, and the brief moments he can interact with fans.

"I like to just feel that feeling of being around the tailgate and the atmosphere," Kelce said. "It's just a part of the ballpark experience. I'm a fan of this game at heart, so getting that feeling of the moment building [before kickoff]. That's all a part of it for me."

Kelce's career has coincided with the Chiefs' most successful period at Arrowhead. His Chiefs teams have won 76.5% of their games in the stadium, including 16 victories in the postseason. Fans inside the venue have also been privileged to see each stage of Kelce's transformation as a player, from a talented-but-sometimes-immature phenom to a certain future Hall of Famer.

"Arrowhead's real magic is when you get inside," Kelce said. "It's something I know I'll cherish forever,

articles.headline: As Nike replaces Adidas, is UEFA Champions League star ball on its way out?
articles.description: Nike will replace Adidas as supplier of UEFA Champions League match balls from next season. Will the famous 'star ball' design soon be no more?
articles.body:
Editor's note: This article was first published on Aug. 26, 2026 and has been updated 

The UEFA Champions League and UEFA Women's Champions League match balls will boast a brand new look starting next season after UEFA confirmed on Monday that Nike will be taking over from long-standing provider Adidas as the official supplier for the 2027-28 campaign onwards.

Nike will take the reins for the 2027-28 campaign onward after agreeing a deal to supply the official match balls for all three UEFA club competitions from 2027 to 2031 -- the Champions League, the Europa League and the Conference League. According to The Guardian, that deal is worth around $45 million a year, double the value of the final contract with Adidas.

- Man United, Pochettino's to-do list based on what's gone wrong

- Meet Como's Paz, the heir to Messi's Argentina No. 10 shirt

- Champions League talking points: Are Como the real deal?

With Adidas having supplied the official Champions League match ball since 2001, the "star ball" design has become an emblem of the competition. However, the last we see of the iconic pattern might be in the 2026-27 final.

That's because, as things stand, there are no specific details available as to the designs that Nike has in store. In a statement on Monday, UEFA would only say: "Further details on the match ball designs will be revealed in due course." It is also unclear -- and highly unlikely -- that the American sportswear giant will continue with the star theme popularised by Adidas over the past 25 years, as the German powerhouse reportedly hold the rights to the star ball design.

Nike's designs are therefore likely to be fresh and distinct with the intent of drawing a line under Adidas' tenure as UEFA match ball suppliers while also launching their own, modernised visual identity.

Back in August, Adidas unveiled what will be their final iteration of the "star ball," the preliminary eye-catching colourway of which is currently being used throughout the group phase of the 2026-27 Champions League.

The men's version of the 2026-27 Champions League ball is plastered in a neon-spattered livery that, according to Adidas, has been inspired by players creating colourful moments of magic and personal expression while plugging away at training on cold, foggy training pitches during their quest to attain Champions League greatness.

The design for the women's match ball is a little less abstract. The golden-orange pattern takes its inspiration from the aura of the ring of 11 stars that make up the UWCL emblem, with flashes of metallic purple and silver then adding a dash of visual contrast to the mix.

Both balls are based on the template that Adidas have used for their Champions League match balls since the introduction of the "Finale 1" ball for the 2001-02 season. articles.headline: Reranking the MVP for each of the top Premier League clubs
articles.description: Based on a simple combination of ability and tactical importance, we've reranked the best players in order at the top Premier League clubs.
articles.body:
In March 2026, we delivered the sixth installment of our Premier League MVP rankings, aimed at tackling a mighty question: Which players rank as the most important at the division's top clubs?

We used a simple combination of ability and tactical factors to assess how crucial the players were to their teams and ranked the top 15 accordingly. Naturally, the best, most consistent and most present players filtered toward the top, while also allowing room for the most tactically crucial individuals to receive credit, too.

Now we've revisited the subject for a seventh installment, intrigued to see how things have changed. Football teams have to weather plenty of storms over the course of half a year, often changing, tweaking and recalibrating around injuries, absences and fluctuations in form.

So, we've reranked the players for another edition -- but this time, there are some major changes to the lineup. Firstly, Tottenham Hotspur have been dropped from the rankings, as they've spent too long circling the drain to warrant inclusion -- some might argue Manchester United deserve the same treatment, but they've hung on for now and, to be fair, they did finish third last season. Secondly, Manchester City's section looks very different as an earnest conversation around them as a club right now feels all but impossible.

Why 15? Well, with 11 first-team players starting any given match, this should allow for those squad positions that aren't 100% cemented. Any long-term injury absences will be noted separately and not considered for the ranking.

Who is eligible? The minimum minutes cutoff is 250 minutes, across Premier League, Champions League and League Cup action, which isn't a particularly high bar. That's in recognition of the fact that amid the increasingly congested schedule, even the top teams have to mix and match their XIs across the competitions to stay healthy.

How did you rate the players? A ranking like this will always be somewhat subjective, but efforts were made to consult experts on each club to help shape the rankings in accordance with our methodology.

Are stats involved? Statistics proved a powerful tool in backing up our assertions, with Opta's data used throughout and Gradient Sports' grades and physical data aiding the process, too. Please note that unless stated otherwise, all referenced statistics such as minutes played, goal contributions and tackles, etc. are a combination of Premier League and Champions League play.

How hard is it? Some of the decisions are glaringly obvious, but others not so much. Comparing players across different position groups is a difficult task. Within the context of a squad, though, it's possible to get a feel for who is the most integral.

I disagree wholeheartedly with your decision to put X below Y. Will you change it? Of course people will disagree, and a lot of this is subjective, but it's only a bit of fun.

Enough of that. On with the rankings.

articles.headline: Mauricio Pochettino's first day at Man United: 'You will see, give me time'
articles.description: Mauricio Pochettino will arrive at Manchester United for his first day as their head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn their fortunes around.
articles.body:
Mauricio Pochettino will arrive at Manchester United for his first day as their head coach on Wednesday but said he requires "time" to turn their fortunes around.

Pochettino's final act in charge of the USMNT was a 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.

He is set to arrive at Carrington on Wednesday as the replacement for the sacked Michael Carrick before his first game leading United on Sunday against Liverpool at Anfield.

On Tuesday night, Pochettino was told by former Manchester City and United States player DaMarcus Beasley that "Manchester is blue, it will always be blue."

He responded: "You will see. Give me time.

"The new challenge is a big challenge, but at the same time it's adrenalin you want to feel. We need to add our common sense... we know the situation is not a situation that deserves to be a club like Manchester United, the fan base is amazing."

Pochettino added: "The mentality is to learn from everyone. You need to have an open mind because I think the players can teach us everyday, we are much better coaching staff now.

"Football is about attitude, and it's about the approach. It's about connection, feelings and communication."

Mauricio Pochettino starts work at Man United on Wednesday

Pochettino was also asked about whether he can improve United's running statistics. United's running was criticised by ex-boss Carrick after a drab 4-1 loss against Como in the Champions League.

In response to Bruno Fernandes' criticism of the team's tactics, Carrick said: "Whatever system you play, whatever tactics you play, if you don't run, and you don't run forward, and you don't run back, you ain't going to win."

Pochettino said on Tuesday night: "What I can talk in general, football is very complex and I think it's not important if you run or not run.

"You need to run well, you need to run with an objective, you need to run together. Then you need to play, you need to know what you need to do, you need to express your talent. The mindsets are so important."

Pochettino led the U.S. to the round of 16 at last summer's World Cup on home soil.

But he is now returning to the Premier League where he has previously coached Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea.

- Mauricio Pochettino can't fix Man United on his own, the owners have to do their jobs

- JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears

- Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at height of Man United career

The former Argentina international, who also coached Lionel Messi, Neymar and Kylian Mbappé at Paris Saint-Germain, takes over at United with the club in the relegation zone after 10 games.

articles.headline: Kansas' Tyran Stokes to undergo MRI after early exit vs. UNLV
articles.description: Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes, the projected No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA draft, left Tuesday's win at UNLV early in the second half.
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS -- Kansas freshman Tyran Stokes, the projected No. 1 pick in the 2027 NBA draft, will undergo an MRI after leaving Tuesday's 102-77 win over UNLV early in the second half.

Stokes sat down on the court with 18:39 left in the game, pointing to the outside of his right knee. He had to be helped off the floor and went straight to the locker room, although he was seen walking under his own power in the hallway.

Following the game, Jayhawks coach Bill Self said Stokes was getting an MRI but that he didn't know the severity of the injury.

"It's a lower leg deal," Self said. "He lost strength in his leg, and that's why he sat down. I don't know anything more than that. So, MRI will probably tell us what the issue is.

"It didn't look bad to me, but sometimes things that don't look bad can be more serious than things that actually do look bad. So, I'll reserve comment on the seriousness because we have no idea."

Stokes, a 6-foot-8 forward and the former No. 1 recruit in the 2026 high school class, logged 13 points and 10 rebounds in just 13 minutes prior to the injury. He's now averaging 14.8 points and 8.0 rebounds through four games, highlighted by a 23-point, 10-rebound, four-assist effort in last week's Champions Classic win over Kentucky.

No. 11 Kansas cruised past UNLV despite Stokes' departure in a game that never featured any drama. The Jayhawks were up by double digits before the first media timeout and led by as many as 38 points in the second half. They made 16 of their first 17 shots from the field and had scored 44 points before missing their second shot of the contest.

Leroy Blyden Jr. led Kansas with 23 points and six assists, and Self highlighted Keanu Dawes and Tre White when asked which players stepped up in Stokes' absence.

"I actually thought Keanu, not offensively, but I thought defensively and from rebounding the ball, I thought he was terrific," Self said. "But if you're going to look at the guys that stepped up offensively after he went down, I'd say more Leroy, [Taylen Kinney] and Tre. Tre is one of those guys, he takes eight shots and gets 15. He's just been very efficient for us. It goes unnoticed."

Kansas will face West Virginia in Wednesday's Players Era 8 semifinal.

articles.headline: Source: Cardinals' Gardner Minshew has surgery to repair right UCL
articles.description: Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II had surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday, a source told ESPN.
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. -- Cardinals quarterback Gardner Minshew II had surgery on his right ulnar collateral ligament on Monday, a source told ESPN.

He is expected to make a full recovery, the source said.

Minshew suffered the injury at the end of the first half of Arizona's Week 9 loss at the Seattle Seahawks. He played the second half but didn't realize the severity of his injury.

He was put on injured reserve two days later, ending his first season with the Cardinals. Minshew signed a one-year deal in March and is scheduled to be a free agent after the season.

Last Wednesday, coach Mike LaFleur said Minshew could tell something was wrong after suffering the injury but his adrenaline was pumping so he couldn't tell how bad it truly was. LaFleur said he was surprised by the news of Minshew's injury.

LaFleur said the injury was "devastating" for Minshew.

"Even on Monday, he felt confident that it wasn't that much until the test came back," LaFleur said.

Minshew threw for 354 yards and three touchdowns on 38-of-53 passing in five full quarters, an overtime and about 95 seconds of the third quarter of Arizona's Week 8 win over the Cowboys.

articles.headline: JJ Gabriel confirms Man United exit as Real Madrid transfer nears
articles.description: JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.
articles.body:
JJ Gabriel has confirmed his departure from Manchester United in a post on Instagram and thanked the club for the role they have played in his career.

The 16-year-old asked to leave United in September and sources told ESPN that he is on the brink of a move to Real Madrid. He had been training in Madrid earlier this month.

"Dear Manchester United, I arrived in 2020 as a 10-year-old boy with big dreams," he said in the video on Instagram.

"Here, I grew as a player and a person. From scoring at Old Trafford to receiving the Jimmy Murphy Award, you gave me moments I'll always treasure.

"To every coach, every member of staff, to my team-mates and everyone who supported me, thank you for believing in me and helping me grow.

"As I begin my next chapter, Manchester United will always be a part of my story. Thank you for everything, JJ."

- Man United's JJ Gabriel amid Real Madrid move talk: 'Dream to win a Ballon d'Or'

- Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at height of Man United career

United will consider legal action if they believe illegal approaches were made while Gabriel was under contract at Old Trafford, sources said.

Gabriel's Irish passport, which allows him to join any club in the European Union, could help facilitate the transfer under FIFA regulations governing international moves for players aged between 16 and 18, with January the first opportunity for him to be registered.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: AC Milan, Juventus eye USMNT's Folarin Balogun
articles.description: AS Monaco and USMNT striker Folarin Balogun is reportedly linked to two of Italy's biggest clubs. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus, while Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw is on the radar of Manchester United. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- AS Monaco striker Folarin Balogun has been offered to AC Milan and Juventus ahead of the January transfer window, Calciomercato has reported. The USMNT striker's agent Jorge Mendes has contacted both clubs, who are looking to strengthen their attacking options, after a €40 million move to Everton collapsed at the end of the last window. The 25-year-old, who is under contract at Monaco until June 2028, is reportedly open to the idea of playing in Serie A.

- Manchester United are among the clubs interested in Newcastle United center back Malick Thiaw, according to Sky Germany. Despite establishing himself as a key figure in the Magpies' backline, the 25-year-old Germany international could be available next summer, although Newcastle would demand at least an €80 million fee for his signature. However, Newcastle will reject any January offers for left back Lewis Hall amid longstanding interest from United, according to The Telegraph. The 22-year-old was the subject of an enquiry from the Red Devils last summer before signing a new long-term contract in September.

- Real Madrid are weighing up a move to bring Brighton & Hove Albion midfielder Chema Andrés back to the club, as per TEAMtalk. Chema, 21, came through the Madrid youth team ranks but left in 2025 and has impressed since arriving at VfB Stuttgart in the summer. However, a deal could be complicated as there is uncertainty over his contractual situation, with Brighton previously disputing suggestions that Madrid retain an option to re-sign him permanently. Madrid also monitoring highly-rated Brighton defender Luka Vuskovic, who joined from Tottenham Hotspur for £46 million this summer.

- Manchester City defender Josko Gvardiol is on the radar of Barcelona, according to AS. Gvardiol, 24, has become one of the best young defenders in Europe in recent years and Barca are keen to strengthen their defensive options. However, while the club are interested in signing the Croatia international, they do not think a deal will be possible unless he pushes to leave amid the fallout from City's financial charges.

- Bayern Munich youth goalkeeper Leonard Prescott could leave  on a free transfer next summer, after contract talks stalled, with Chelsea, Arsenal, Brighton and Aston Villa are among the clubs tracking his development, says Sky Germany. Prescott, 17, was born in New York but has represented Germany at U17 and is very highly rated.

OTHERS

- Chelsea are lining up a double swoop for Barcelona stars Fermín López and Jules Koundé, and could submit a €150 million offer for both players in January. (El Nacional)

articles.headline: Matheus Nunes in talks to extend Man City deal - sources
articles.description: Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester City are in talks with Matheus Nunes about extending his contract at the Etihad Stadium, sources have told ESPN.

Nunes has a deal until 2028, but City are keen to agree fresh terms. Negotiations are ongoing, although sources have told ESPN that talks are not yet at an advanced stage.

The Portugal international is closing in on 150 appearances for the club after arriving from Wolves in 2023. Initially joining as a midfielder, he was converted to a full-back under former boss Pep Guardiola.

Nunes appeared in 34 of City's 38 Premier League games last season with his form convincing club bosses to strengthen other areas of the squad over the summer instead of at right-back.

Meanwhile, City are facing a decision about whether to keep midfielder Mateo Kovacic. The Croatian is out of contract at the end of the season and can negotiate with clubs outside the Premier League from January.

Kovacic has struggled for game time so far this season and has made just one Premier League start under new manager Enzo Maresca.

articles.headline: Oviedo fan handed suspended prison sentence for racist abuse toward Mbappé
articles.description: A person has been given a suspended 11-month prison sentence as well a stadium ban and fined for racist insults directed toward Real Madrid forward Kylian Mbappé during a LaLiga match at Real Oviedo in August.
